/-!
# Erdős Problem 1065

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1065](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1065)
-/

namespace Erdos1065

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k * q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$?

This is mentioned as B46
in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
 -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * q + 1} := by
  sorry

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k 3^l q + 1$
for some prime $q$ and $k ≥ 0$, $l ≥ 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1065.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    Set.Infinite {p | ∃ q k l, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p = 2^k * 3^l * q + 1} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1065

reformulations.difference: Guy's B46 asks whether (p−1)/P(p−1) is a power of 2 for infinitely many primes p, where P denotes the largest prime factor. Lean instead uses p = 2^k*q + 1 with q prime, matching the website's wording.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For p>2, a factorization p−1=2^k*q makes q the largest prime factor, since q≥2. Thus the quotient is 2^k. Conversely, take q=P(p−1) and multiply the quotient identity by q. Any convention-dependent inclusion of p=2 is a finite difference and cannot affect infinitude. The full infinitude equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean without sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: Guy's B46 uses (p−1)/P(p−1)=2^k*3^l. Lean instead existentially factors p−1 as 2^k*3^l*q for an arbitrary prime q, again matching the website.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For p>2, if q≥3 it is the largest prime factor. If q=2 and l=0, the largest prime factor is 2 and the quotient is 2^k. If q=2 and l>0, the largest prime factor is 3 and the quotient is 2^(k+1)*3^(l−1), still of the required form. Conversely, choose q=P(p−1) and multiply the quotient identity by q. The possible boundary discrepancy at p=2 does not affect infinitude. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean without sorry dependencies.
